description: This bar chart illustrates five distinct layer grouping patterns—labeled “Increasing,” “Uniform,” “Decreasing,” “Spindle,” and “Bottleneck”—each depicted as a horizontal arrangement of four light green bars representing groups G₁ through G₄. The horizontal axis serves as the category axis, with each pattern’s label positioned beneath its corresponding set of bars, while the vertical axis represents the number of layers in each group, though its specific scale is not labeled or numerically marked. Within each pattern, the bars are arranged sequentially from left to right (G₁ to G₄), and their heights visually encode the number of layers assigned to each group. For the “Increasing” pattern, the bars rise progressively from left to right, with approximate heights of 1, 2, 3, and 4 layers respectively. The “Uniform” pattern shows four bars of equal height, each representing 2 layers. In the “Decreasing” pattern, the bars fall progressively from left to right, with approximate heights of 4, 3, 2, and 1 layer. The “Spindle” pattern features two tall central bars (each approximately 3 layers) flanked by two shorter bars (each approximately 1 layer). The “Bottleneck” pattern displays two tall bars (each approximately 3 layers) on the outer positions (G₁ and G₄) and two shorter bars (each approximately 1 layer) in the center (G₂ and G₃). The bars are not sorted by height, and no visual emphasis such as shading, bolding, or annotations is applied to any specific bar or group.
